svg.title: GenAI-GE architecture: an ECS game whose entities, components and systems are invented at runtime by a six agent LLM pipeline
svg.text: GenAI-GE: an engine that writes its own rules
A 76 line renderer that understands only text, circles and rectangles is the entire hard coded game. Every entity, component and system inside it is
invented and executed by language models at runtime, in response to whatever the player types. Six agents, fixed order, one pass per turn.
Invented by an LLM at runtime, per turn
Free text. No verb list, no command
"let's duel! make the board with 6 places
server.js: Express + Socket.IO · aiManager.processPlayerInput() builds the turn state and calls graph.invoke({ state }, { recursionLimit: 50 })
aiGraph.js: a LangGraph StateGraph of six nodes. The router is a hand written if/else on state.sender. The order below is fixed, never chosen.
Every node mutates one shared mutable state object; nothing is returned to the caller except that object.
This file, the renderer, and a five case switch are the whole engine. Everything else in this diagram is text a model produced.
A conventional engine hard codes systems and lets content vary. This one
inverts that: the only fixed things are five ways to mutate state and three
shapes to draw. When the player asks for a card game, no card system is
loaded: one is written, in prose, and then executed by a model reading it.
The engine never learns what a card is. It only ever moves components around.
One string, prepended verbatim to all six system prompts. The only game design in the repository that a human wrote.
systems described in prose, not code
• The render contract: shape | text, color,
• Three worked examples with exact JSON:

before it answers. Also receives every entity and
the full transcript of previous turns as text.

A system is a paragraph of English. "logic" is the
entire implementation: it is handed back to the
resolver as its instructions two steps later.

This is where "systems" actually run: the model is
told "you are the <systemName> Resolver AI" and
given the system's own prose as its rules.

Applies everything pending, pushes state to the
client, sleeps 1s, asks for a new capture, sleeps 3s.
Then compares two images, the pre-turn frame and
the new one, and is asked to make the board
legible: bigger text, no overlaps, visible entities.
Reads systemResults and the current state, not the
GameMaster's directive, so it can describe a
different outcome from the one the turn opened with.
That divergence is visible in the traced turn.
systems are appended, never removed ⚑ note 1
read in full, every turn → N LLM calls
stateChanges[] from agents 1, 3, 4 and 5, applied in that order, all through one switch
The complete list of things this engine can do to a world:
• create_entity ignores parameters.entityName and mints a fresh uuid, a name the model gives an entity is not an address it can reuse.
• add/update_component matches on id, else falls back to role: e.components.player for "player", e.components.enemy for "enemy".
• Called twice per turn: once inside CanvasAdjusterAI to produce a frame, once at the end of processPlayerInput.
No validation, no rollback, no transaction. If a payload is malformed it is written anyway.
live only as prose in activeSystems and only
• The seed world is the only hand authored
• Components are plain objects, any shape a
• fs.writeFile of the whole history, every turn.
• On boot the last entry becomes the world.
rows, 536 KB. It is the proof the thing ran.
• Entries hold live references, so component
values in the file are end of session, not per turn.
PHASER CLIENT · the hard coded half
• 800×600 canvas, a 32 px grid drawn once at startup.
• GameManager.updateRenderComponent() is 76 lines and is the entire renderer:
it walks renderElements and draws text, circles, rectangles and squares. Nothing else.
• zIndex → depth, offset → x/y, alpha, outlineColor. World position × 32 = pixels.
• It has no concept of a card, a deck, a duel, or a turn. It cannot: those words only
ever exist inside strings the models wrote.
• Sidebar: transcript of every agent output + a live JSON state inspector.
⚑ note 2 · the "Save Game State" button here has no handler
The server never handles pixels; it passes an https URL
to the vision model. Synchronisation is a fixed sleep:
1 s for the client to redraw, 3 s for the upload.
This is what makes the loop closed: the game looks at itself.
narration → transcript. router then returns END (aiGraph.js:21): one pass per turn, no retries, no branching
PNG URL of the frame just drawn ↑
PNG URL of the board as it stands, fetched at the start of every turn, so the GameMaster reasons about what the player can actually see

every turn, for the rest of the session.
